title: Tree shaking and dependency cost
description: Learn about Tree shaking and dependency cost. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Tree shaking and dependency cost analysis are essential for optimizing bundle sizes. Tree shaking removes unused code from bundles, while understanding dependency costs helps you make informed decisions about which libraries to include in your application.

Tree shaking is a build optimization technique that eliminates dead code from your bundles. It analyzes the dependency graph and removes exports that are never imported, reducing bundle size without changing functionality.

Tree shaking relies on ES modules (ESM) because they have a static structure that allows build tools to analyze dependencies at build time. CommonJS modules cannot be tree-shaken because their dependencies are determined at runtime.

data.text: Modules with side effects (code that affects global state when imported) cannot be safely tree-shaken. You can mark modules as side-effect-free using the sideEffects field in package.json.

data.title: Package.json Side Effects
data.content: Mark your library as side-effect-free for better tree shaking.

data.text: Understanding the cost of dependencies helps you make informed decisions about which libraries to use. Some libraries are deceptively small but pull in massive dependency trees.

data.title: Bundle Size Analysis Tools
data.content: Use tools to analyze dependency costs.
data.code:
# Install bundle analysis tools
npm install -g cost-of-modules
npm install -g import-cost

# Analyze dependency costs
cost-of-modules ./src

# Webpack bundle analyzer
npm install --save-dev webpack-bundle-analyzer

# Next.js built-in analyzer
ANALYZE=true npm run build

items: **Lodash**: Full library is 70KB (use lodash-es or individual imports)
**Material-UI**: Large bundle size (use tree-shaking or lighter alternatives)
**Immutable.js**: Heavy library (consider immer or native JS)

data.title: Optimized Lodash Usage
data.content: Import only needed functions from lodash.

data.title: Replace Moment.js with date-fns

data.text: Regularly audit your dependencies to remove unused packages. This reduces both bundle size and potential security vulnerabilities.

data.title: Dependency Audit Tools
data.code:
# Find unused dependencies
npm install -g depcheck
depcheck

# Find unused files in codebase
npm install -g unimported
unimported

# Analyze bundle for unused code
npm install -g webpack-bundle-analyzer
webpack-bundle-analyzer dist/static/js/*.js

items: Use ES modules (import/export) instead of CommonJS (require)
Avoid side effects in module-level code
Export individual functions rather than single objects
Use pure functions that don't modify global state
Prefer named exports over default exports for better tree shaking

data.title: Default Export Limitations
data.text: Default exports can limit tree shaking effectiveness. Named exports are generally better because they allow more precise import analysis.

data.title: Named vs Default Exports
data.content: Prefer named exports for better tree shaking.

data.text: Set up automated dependency monitoring in your CI/CD pipeline to catch size regressions and identify problematic dependencies before they reach production.

terms.definition: Build optimization that removes unused code from bundles by analyzing static module dependencies.
Code that affects global state when imported, preventing safe tree shaking of the module.
The total bundle size impact of including a library, including its transitive dependencies.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Tree shaking removes unused code from bundles to reduce size
ES modules enable tree shaking; CommonJS does not
Mark side-effect-free modules in package.json for better optimization
Analyze dependency costs before adding new libraries
Replace heavy libraries with lighter alternatives (moment.js → date-fns)
Import only what you need from large libraries (lodash)
Prefer named exports over default exports for better tree shaking
Regularly audit and remove unused dependencies
data.takeaway: Tree shaking and dependency cost analysis are essential for maintaining optimal bundle sizes and preventing unnecessary bloat in your applications.
